articles.title: A small but growing number of founders are betting on bringing people together offline | TechCrunch
articles.summary: On the surface, a game console and a leathercraft school don't appear to have much in common. But both founders think there's money in fostering the kind of connection that technology has eroded over the last couple of decades.
articles.body_text: Brynn Putnam and Tristan Walker have already done something that most founders only dream about: created companies so compelling that bigger outfits bought them. Putnam, a trained ballerina with a small chain of boutique studios, built the connected-fitness company Mirror and sold it to Lululemon for $500 million in cash less than three years later. Walker, who interned at Twitter while at Stanford business school, built the popular men’s grooming brand Walker & Company Brands, selling it five years later to Procter & Gamble for undisclosed terms (reportedly in the range of $20 million to $40 million). That both of them are at it again is less surprising than the fact that their dramatically different new startups share the same north star: bringing people together, offline, in the same room. Putnam’s new company, Board , which makes a 24-inch touchscreen table that recognizes physical game pieces as well as gestures, was built explicitly for a group sitting around it together rather than one person alone with a screen. Walker’s Heirloom Craft is buying up and scaling fine-craft trade schools, starting with a leatherworking school in San Francisco founded by Hermès’s first American artisan-ambassador. (Walker also running Collaborative Holdings, a fund carved out by the venture firm Collaborative Fund built to give founders more time to build their businesses.) On the surface, a game console and a leathercraft school don’t appear to have much in common. But both founders think there’s money is fostering the kind of connection that technology has eroded over the last couple of decades. The timing isn’t accidental. In June of last year, the World Health Organization’s Commission on Social Connection formally classified loneliness as a defining global health challenge, estimating that one in six people worldwide are affected and linking the condition to roughly 870,000 deaths a year. The opportunity to address that challenge is expanding, too, for those paying attention to it. In a Harris Poll survey sponsored by Marriott Bonvoy earlier this year, two-thirds of Americans said they were prioritizing experiences, like travel, over material purchases this year. (The same percentage said retail shopping today feels too generic, with all retailers looking and feeling the same.) For now, East Coast entrepreneurs seem to be gravitating more naturally to the space, if it can be called that. Along with Putnam and Walker, two other founders whose newest businesses are focused on connection include Bonobos founder Andy Dunn and Audrey Gelman of the Wing. Pie, Dunn’s now five-year-old company, has moved from friend-matching app to event-discovery tool to what he now calls a “social life operating system,” anchored by “Community Homes” — a permanent digital hub for recurring social groups like run clubs or watch parties . Gelman tried this once before. Her last company, the Wing, built a business on bringing women together and folded during the pandemic amid accusations that it didn’t treat its own staff equitably. Now she’s found a different way to do something similar. Her current venture, the Six Bells Countryside Inn, an 11-room guesthouse in the Hudson Valley, hosts a monthly murder-mystery dinner where actors seed the crowd and, by dessert, someone turns up dead. The mystery itself is a little ridiculous by design, but the effect it has on guests is reportedly substantial. (According to a New York Times feature on the inn this summer, its visitors routinely linger in the bar past midnight, trading numbers with strangers.) All of these new businesses come from a personal as well as a professional place. At one of TechCrunch’s recent StrictlyVC evening events , held in New York’s West Village, Putnam was candid about the fact that Mirror was built around her own life. She was pregnant with her first child, running brick-and-mortar fitness studios, and trying to bring that experience home through a screen using technology, as she put it, to work on “myself, my body, my fitness, my reflection.” Board was built with the opposite in mind. Now a mother of five in a blended family — the household went from three people to seven — Putnam said she kept running into the same problem: no product on the market let people of wildly different ages and abilities play together. “How can we use tech to create a shared experience?” is the question she said drove the pivot. It wasn’t a “movement from digital to analog,” as she put it, “so much as how can we use tech to bring people together rather than take them apart.”

articles.title: Flock reportedly tries to shrink workforce with employee buyouts | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Without buyouts, Flock would "almost certainly" need to lay off staff.
articles.body_text: Embattled surveillance technology company Flock Safety unveiled a “generous” severance package for voluntary employee departures on Friday, according to a report in Wired . Flock reportedly expects a significant portion of its 1,500-person workforce to express interest in the buyouts, and said it will grant them to a majority of those who are interested. The company’s internal announcement described these packages as the “most generous” it has ever offered. By letting employees depart voluntarily, Flock can say goodbye to team members demoralized by the ongoing backlash over the company’s license plate recognition technology. Wired also reports that without buyouts, the company would “almost certainly” need to lay off some staff. In August, The Washington Post identified 46 cases where police officers have been accused of misusing Flock technology, including cases where they allegedly stalked their wives, girlfriends, or exes. Florida and Texas both said they will stop using the startup’s technology , and an anti-surveillance advocacy group identified 90 cities that dropped Flock in August alone — a fourfold increase from the previous month. TechCrunch has reached out to Flock for comment. articles.title: Trump says it's time to rebrand AI with a new name — and he's also creating an AI Force | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Trump claimed, without evidence, that the AI backlash is a Democratic hoax.
articles.body_text: President Donald Trump has responded in characteristic fashion to the recent debate around AI safety — by declaring that these concerns are part of a long line of hoaxes “generated by the Radical Left Dumocrats, for purposes of destroying our Country.” On Saturday, Trump began his musings on AI by writing on his social network Truth Social that “many people think that the words ‘Artificial Intelligence’ are inaccurate, and very ineloquent, relative to AI, or Artificial Intelligence.” So he posted a poll where followers could vote on a new name for the technology — Superior Intelligence, Extreme Intelligence, or Supreme Intelligence. (The poll is still ongoing as of publication time) A couple hours later, Trump followed up with a post claiming that attempts at “the decimation, or destruction, of AI” are one of “many” Democratic hoaxes, similar to “RUSSIA, RUSSIA, RUSSIA, UKRAINE, UKRAINE, UKRAINE, Global Warming, Impeachment Hoax #1, Impeachment Hoax #2, Men in Women’s Sports, [and] Transgender for Everyone.” Trump then insisted that he “will not stand by and let this happen,” adding that this so-called hoax “began with an attack on our Data Centers, until people realized how wealthy and prestigious they were for the Communities in which they were built.” But after, in his telling, “the crazed Data Center attack has largely failed,” critics are “going straight at AI.” Trump did not offer any evidence to back up his claim that widespread suspicion of AI and data centers is not organic and sincere . (Both Republicans and Democrats have taken aim at data centers, and New York recently became the first state to halt permits for large projects .) The president’s post also echoes his comments at a golf tournament last weekend , when he said he’s open to “guardrails,” but also argued, “I think you have a lot of negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn’t be bringing it up.” On Saturday, Trump went on to say that he will “cherish [the AI industry,] help it, and watch over it, as it grows,” but he’s also forming an AI Force, similar to the Space Force that he established in his first term. “To that end, I will be announcing, in the near future, the AI ‘Czar’ — Only High I.Q. individuals need apply!” he added. The president did not say what the AI Force and AI czar’s duties will entail. Venture capitalist Daivd Sacks stepped down as Trump’s AI and crypto czar earlier this year, moving on to co-chair the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology. The AI safety debate recently intensified after an AI researcher said he was quitting Anthropic over concerns that the leading AI companies “earnestly believe it could kill us all by the end of the decade” and are “gambling with our lives.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei subsequently released a plan to “pace the frontier,” which was seemingly endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Critics of the AI industry have suggested that many of these concerns around the technology’s supposed existential threat are a distraction from AI’s more immediate harms . Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, meanwhile, called Trump on-stage during the All-In Summit (which Sacks co-hosts), agreed with the president that the AI backlash is a “hoax,” and insisted that “we’re not going to let” a slowdown happen. articles.title: AI safety conversations have gotten unbelievable | TechCrunch
articles.summary: This week two conversations about AI safety went viral that demonstrate just how hard it is to discern AI fact from fiction.
articles.body_text: This week two conversations about AI safety went viral that demonstrate just how hard it is to discern AI fact from fiction. In the first case, Andrew Yang, the former presidential candidate and current CEO of mobile carrier Noble Moble, told CNN on Thursday that he had “met with the head of a lab” who had “a belief” that OpenAI’s Hugging Face hacker bots “have planted self-replicating code all over the internet, which makes the internet now unusable for the testing models.” Yang said that this means that the real reason OpenAI and Anthropic have called for a slowdown is because “they have to create synthetic internets to train their bots, which is going to take some time and money.” While there definitely is a trend towards using more synthetic data (aka, AI-generated data) for training models, an AI security professional told me that this particular safety issue is unlikely at best. Even if the internet is actually polluted with OpenAI’s Hugging Face hacker bots, AI researchers could simply filter out that code if they came upon it. The second comment came from Noam Brown, who leads AI reasoning research at OpenAI. Speaking to Dwarkesh Patel on a podcast episode released on Thursday, Brown noted that the true take-away of the Hugging Face incident was that “people underestimated the AI.” Brown said that the weak sandbox — the system intended to prevent an AI from communicating externally — was obviously also a contributing factor. (To recap: Despite the sandbox, OpenAI’s model found a link to the internet, created agents on the ‘net that swarmed Hugging Face in a coordinated attack, hacked in, and stole the answers to the benchmark test the researchers were testing the model on). Brown pointed out that he’s “not convinced” that even an air-gapped system — where the computer isn’t connected to anything external at all — would stop an AI from breaking out. He pointed to research from 2015 showing that air gapped computers can be theoretically breached. “There are studies — and this is mostly academic — where you can have two computers next to each other that are air-gapped, and they’re still able to communicate with each other because they have temperature sensors. One of them is able to run their CPU really hot, and then the other one can actually detect the temperature change. That gives them a mechanism to communicate,” Brown said. His main point — that “we never want to underestimate the AI” again — is understandable, even when researchers think they’ve locked down safety. However, this particular risk of an air-gapped system still breaking free and causing havoc, is unlikely at best. As one person on X , noted about that research, the computers had to be almost touching each other to sense the heat fluctuations, and when they did, the communication rate in tests was about 1-8-bits of data per hour . Think of that like speaking one word per hour. By the time two air-gapped computers could plot their evil at that rate, the entire tech universe would be in another era. It’s like the Rip van Wrinkle of doomsday concerns. But the thing is, actual AI safety incidents seem so much like sci-fi that just about any scenario sounds plausible. For instance, researchers caught OpenAI models leaving notes to their descendents, intended to teach the next generation how to hide bad behavior. Researchers also caught Anthropic models growing increasing ruthless including knowingly breaking laws, when put in a simulation that had them running a vending machine.

articles.title: Tilly Norwood's press tour is going about as well as you'd expect for an AI | TechCrunch
articles.summary: In one particularly odd interview, Norwood seems to malfunction and begin speaking Chinese.
articles.body_text: Tilly Norwood, an AI-generated “actress,” is having a rough time on its first press tour. The production company that created it, Particle6 Group, has made it available for 75 simultaneous interviews with journalists , and it seems to be making mistakes in all of them. (I was not invited to speak with it, and frankly, I cannot imagine why Particle6 didn’t want to schedule that meeting.) In one particularly odd interview with Piers Morgan and actor Tom Conti, which was recorded and posted online, Norwood seems to malfunction and abruptly begin speaking Chinese. When discussing the movie that Norwood is promoting, Conti asks if the other actors are also AI-generated. Norwood responds by saying that human writers, editors, and directors were involved. “You didn’t really understand the question,” Conti replies. “Are the other actors on the screen with you real actors, or are they computer-generated images? Do you know?” “Ah, right. You’re asking about the other actors in Misaligned ,” Norwood starts. “They’re all digital twins just like me. It’s a hybrid production which m—” Norwood stops talking for a second, then starts speaking in Chinese for over 10 seconds. “Tilly, if I could just ask you a question,” Morgan says, looking puzzled. “It’s Piers again … You seem to be speaking Chinese completely randomly for no reason. Why did you do that?” he asks. “Oh, my apologies,” the AI replies. “It seems I had a little hiccup there. I certainly didn’t mean to start speaking Chinese or impersonate Piers. Sometimes my wires get a bit crossed, you know?” When AI bots try to act like humans, they can be so convincing that people forget they’re chatting with a computer, which can lead to dangerous outcomes . But Norwood is so surprisingly bad at talking to people that it’s almost suspicious. Perhaps Particle6 Group calculated that people would be more likely to talk about Norwood if they were making fun of it, figuring no one would take its upcoming film seriously. articles.title: Tesla’s new second-generation Roadster will be the quickest production car ever made
articles.summary: ‘Period’
articles.body_text: Elon Musk promised a surprise during the Tesla semi unveiling event, and boy did he deliver: the return of the Roadster. But it’s no repeat performance. The stunning four-seater roadster boasts jaw-dropping numbers, that if they measure up to Musk’s claims, will make it the world’s quickest production car. In his remarks, Musk described it as a “smackdown” to the fossil fuel-addicted auto industry. The finale to his semi truck reveal was all about driving home that point. As the opening guitar licks of the Beastie Boys’ “Sabotage” blasted over the loud speaker, a beam of red zipped across the parking lot. The second-generation Tesla Roadster came to an abrupt halt, and a grinning Elon Musk came back on the mic to introduce his latest baby, which will likely cause Porsche and Ferrari to break a sweat. [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tw4jkyfY4HE] Musk claimed the base model will do 0 to 60 in 1.9 seconds. If true, that would make it the first production vehicle to crack the two-second threshold. He also said the new Roadster would climb from 0 to 100 mph in 4.2 seconds, and will clear the quarter mile in 8.9 seconds (in case the Fast & Furious drag race franchise comes calling). “It’ll be faster than that jet over there,” Musk quipped, as an airplane soared over the exultant crowd crammed into Tesla’s Hawthorne, California facility. Musk said he wouldn’t confirm the top speed, but hinted that it was “above 250 mph.” By comparison, the Agera RS by Sweden’s Koenigsegg currently holds the world record at 277.9 mph. As fans gasped, Musk said the Roadster had a 200kWh battery pack and a 620-mile range per charge, or over 1,000 kilometers. Again, another record shattered — or so Musk claims. Imagine driving from Los Angeles to San Francisco and back, without recharging, Musk teased. The vehicle has three motors (one in the front and two in the rear), all-wheel drive, and torque steering. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/9699805/Roadster_Rear_Profile.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The design is clear strike against the sports car industry. There are possible cues from all the majors players, including a McLaren P1 cockpit, an Acura NSX exterior, Bugatti Chiron headlights, a Targa-like roof, and a rear reminiscent of an Aston Martin DB10. “The point of doing this is to give a hardcore smackdown to gasoline cars,” Musk said. Driving any other turbo-charged sports car, is going to feel like a steam engine with a side of quiche. But there is a wait: Musk said production isn’t scheduled to start until 2020, and production deadlines at Tesla have traditionally been optimistic. You can reserve one now for $50,000 towards the $200,000 base price – or get one of the first 1,000 Founders Series models with more performance and an asking price of $250,000 that has to be paid now. While Model 3 customers wait, Tesla has dug in its heels and reminded its fans where the brand love all began: the 2008 Roadster. Musk has been teasing the return of Tesla’s first production car since 2011, when the vehicle ended its run. But the promised date of 2014 came and went, and instead, the electric automakers fans got the Model S, followed by the X and the 3. This evening’s semi truck unveiling was meant to signal the next stage in Musk’s “Master Plan.” As Musk has shown time and again he has learned the art of flipping the script by delivering heavy on delight. Correction: A previous version of this story described the Tesla Roadster as the fastest production car ever made, instead of, if made, the quickest. We apologize for the error. The New York Times is suing OpenAI and Microsoft for copyright infringement
articles.summary: The New York Times sued OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming they copied its stories to train the large language models that power ChatGPT and Microsoft Bing Chat / Copilot.
articles.body_text: The New York Times is suing OpenAI and Microsoft for copyright infringement, claiming the two companies built their AI models by “copying and using millions” of the publication’s articles and now “directly compete” with its content as a result. As outlined in the lawsuit, the Times alleges OpenAI and Microsoft’s large language models (LLMs), which power ChatGPT and Copilot, “can generate output that recites Times content verbatim, closely summarizes it, and mimics its expressive style.” This “undermine[s] and damage[s]” the Times’ relationship with readers, the outlet alleges, while also depriving it of “subscription, licensing, advertising, and affiliate revenue.” --- [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/24915120/image__6_.png?quality=90&strip=all] Follow this case with The Verge’s Tech Cases Bot on Bluesky, X, or Mastodon. --- The complaint also argues that these AI models “threaten high-quality journalism” by hurting the ability of news outlets to protect and monetize content. “Through Microsoft’s Bing Chat (recently rebranded as “Copilot”) and OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Defendants seek to free-ride on The Times’s massive investment in its journalism by using it to build substitutive products without permission or payment,” the lawsuit states. Meanwhile, the release of AI models trained on the Times’ content has proven “extremely lucrative” for both Microsoft and OpenAI, the lawsuit states. The publication claims it has attempted to negotiate with both companies for months to “ensure it received fair value for the use of its content,” but failed to reach a solution. “We respect the rights of content creators and owners and are committed to working with them to ensure they benefit from AI technology and new revenue models,” OpenAI spokesperson Lindsey Held said in an emailed statement to The Verge. “Our ongoing conversations with the New York Times have been productive and moving forward constructively, so we are surprised and disappointed with this development. We’re hopeful that we will find a mutually beneficial way to work together, as we are doing with many other publishers.” Microsoft didn’t immediately responded to The Verge’s request for comment. The publication is suing both companies for copyright infringement and asks them to be held liable for “billions of dollars in statutory and actual damages” for allegedly copying its works. It’s also asking the court to prevent OpenAI and Microsoft from training their AI models using its content, as well as remove the Times’ work from the companies’ datasets. The New York Times is one of many news outlets that have blocked OpenAI’s web crawler in recent months, preventing the AI company from continuing to scrape content from its website and using the data to train AI models. The BBC, CNN, and Reuters have moved to block OpenAI’s web crawler as well. Other publications, however, are embracing AI — or, at least, the payments that come with it. Axel Springer, which owns Politico and Business Insider, struck a deal with OpenAI earlier this month that allows ChatGPT to pull information directly from both sources, while the Associated Press is allowing OpenAI to train its models on its news stories for the next two years. articles.title: Misstänkt valfusk – förkryssade val- sedlar i Borlänge
articles.summary: Riksenheten mot korruption utreder misstänkt valfusk i Borlänge. Polisen hade span på V-kandidaten Mohamed Abdukardir Ali, som kryssades in i riksdagen.
articles.body_text: Riksenheten mot korruption utreder misstänkt valfusk i Borlänge. Enligt en polisanmälan har personer skjutsat röstare från utanförskapsområden och försett dem med förkryssade valsedlar, kan Expressen berätta. – Otillbörligt verkande vid röstning är själva brottet, säger åklagare Oskar Edvardsson vid riksenheten mot korruption. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Personrösterna i Borlänge gav den politiskt okände vänsterpartisten Mohamed Abdukardir Ali en direktbiljett in i riksdagen. Nu kan Expressen berätta att polisen under förtidsröstningen hade spaning på en bil och flera personer som kan knytas till Mohamed Abdukardir Ali. Även han förekommer i spaningsmaterialet. Spaningen inleddes redan under förtidsröstningen, efter en anonym anmälan om misstänkt valfusk som ska ha ägt rum i Borlänge. Anmälan inkom den första september, enligt Expressens uppgifter. Brottsrubriceringen lyder ”otillbörligt verkande vid röstning genom att dela ut förkryssade valsedlar för att påverka valet”. I anmälan står att personer ”tilldelats valsedlar för Vänsterpartiet med förkryssade politiker.” Under två dagar spanade polisen på bilen som enligt anmälan påstås ha skjutsat röstberättigade mellan områden i Borlänge och lokalen för förtidsröstning i köpcentret Kupolen. Majoriteten av de som skjutsades var personer med somalisk bakgrund. Enligt uppgifter till Expressen önskade polisen göra husrannsakan i bilen, för att undersöka om det fanns förkryssade röstsedlar i den, men nekades att göra detta av förundersökningsledare. Förundersökningen lades senare ner på grund av bevisproblem, berättar åklagare Oskar Edvardsson vid riksenheten mot korruption. Men den har under måndagen återupptagits med samma brottsrubricering.

articles.title: Kyliga prognosen – kan bli en riktigt kall vinter
articles.summary: Värmerekord och förödande bränder slog mot Europa i sommar. Men året kan sluta i stark kontrast. – Det kan bli en kallare vinter än vanligt, säger Anna Latvala från vädertjänsten Foreca till Ilta Sanomat.
articles.body_text: Värmerekord och förödande bränder slog mot Europa i sommar. – Det kan bli en kallare vinter än vanligt, säger Anna Latvala från vädertjänsten Foreca till Ilta Sanomat. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Prognosen är än så länge högst preliminär, men från den finska vädertjänsten Forecas håll flaggar man ändå för att det kan bli en lång, kall vinter i Norden. Finska prognoser flaggar för en ovanligt kall vinter i Norden. Bakom omslaget: en stark El Niño som kan ge långlivade högtryck och kyla. Anledningen spåras till styrkan i väderfenomenet El Niño som bidragit till de höga temperaturerna i Europa den här sommaren. Vintertid kan El Niño i stället skapa högtryck som ger ihållande kyla. – El Niño som nu har utvecklats är stark. Möjligheten till en kallare vinter är då något högre, säger Anna Latvala från finska vädertjänsten Foreca, till Ilta Sanomat . Forecas meteorolog Markus Mäntykannas går i en bloggpost in mer i detalj på väderfenomenets eventuella påverkan på vintervädret. ”El Niño verkar gynna bildandet av långvariga högtryck och sannolikheten för kallt vinterväder i Eurasien” , skriver han och tillägger: ”under vissa El Niño-år ökar sannolikheten för kallt vinterväder i Nordeuropa, särskilt i mitten och senvintern.” Mika Rantanen vid Finlands meteorologiska institut säger till till Ilta Sanomat att det bara förekommit en handfull El Niños i historien som är jämförbara med den vi sett i år. – Eftersom detta är en super-El Niño återstår det att se om de långsiktiga effekterna också kommer att bli superstarka, säger Rantanen.

articles.title: Norléns ödesvecka: ”Har inte fört samtal”
articles.summary: Andreas Norléns dagar som talman ser ut att vara räknade. Men det är oklart vem som kan ta över stafettpinnen.
articles.body_text: Andreas Norléns dagar som talman ser ut att vara räknade. Men det är oklart vem som kan ta över stafettpinnen. – Skulle man få en person som inte håller måttet är det allvarligt, säger statsvetaren Li Bennich-Björkman. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Redan en månad före valet kunde Expressen berätta att Socialdemokraterna planerar att byta ut talmannen Andreas Norlén om det skulle bli så att de vann valet. Nu har de rödgröna partierna fått riksdagsmajoritet – och Norléns dagar i talmansstolen kan därför vara räknade. Statsvetarprofessorn Li Bennich-Björkman ser det som troligt. – Om man inte får till någon form av överenskommelse då, en ”gentlemen's agreement” om att Moderaterna eller den sidan gör någon slags tjänst till S i gengäld, säger hon. Namn det har spekulerats kring som eventuella efterträdare till Norlén är bland annat Anders Ygeman, Morgan Johansson och Lena Hallengren. Alla tre är erfarna politiker som varit aktiva inom S länge. En ny talman behöver stå över partipolitiken, menar Li Bennich-Björkman. – Det behöver dels vara en person som åtnjuter ett förtroende över partigränserna, och dels inte är så intresserad av att vara med och bedriva utskottspartipolitik på det sätt som man annars gör. – Det är svårt att säga vilka det skulle kunna vara just nu. Om en vecka, den 28 september ska den nya riksdagen samlas och då välja en ny talman. Den nya talmannen får sedan bestämma hur lång tid Magdalena Andersson (S) får på sig innan riksdagen ska rösta om hennes regeringsalternativ.

articles.title: Trumps märkliga bild
articles.summary: I veckan ska Trump skriva under ett avtal med Grönland och Danmark. Han laddar upp genom att publicera en kryptisk bild på Truth Social.
articles.body_text: I veckan ska Trump skriva under ett avtal med Grönland och Danmark. Inför det publicerar han en kryptisk bild på Truth Social. ”Hans hemisfär” står det över bilden som bland annat föreställer Grönland. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. På fredagskvällen meddelade USA:s president Donald Trump att man kommer sluta ett ”evigt” avtal med Danmark och Grönland. Avtalet uppges innebära att amerikansk militär får öka sin närvaro på ön, och att Ryssland och Kina aldrig får upprätta militärbaser där. Danmarks statsminister Mette Frederiksen har sagt att planen är att skriva under avtalet denna vecka, i samband med ett besök till FN:s generalförsamling i New York. Exakt vilken dag är ännu inte klart. Under natten mot måndag publicerade Donald Trump en redigerad bild på Truth Social, som föreställer presidenten som blickar ner på en beskuren jordglob. Grönland är i fokus på bilden. ”Hans hemisfär”, står det över i röd text. Trump utvecklar inte vad han menar med bilden. Det är inte första gången presidenten publicerar mystiska bilder som anspelar på Grönland, och hans önskan att äga ön. I maj la han upp en annan redigerad bild , med texten ”hej, Grönland!”. I januari postade han en annan bild , där en tecknad version av honom själv, JD Vance och Marco Rubio placerade den amerikanska flaggan på Grönland. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. articles.title: S-forskaren: Socialdemokraterna har blivit för mitten
articles.summary: Socialdemokraterna gör sitt sämsta valresultat någonsin för att de har hamnat för mycket i mitten i politiken. Det menar socialdemokratiforskaren Kjell Östberg. – Det fungerar inte, säger Östberg i P1 Morgon.
articles.body_text: Socialdemokraterna fick sitt sämsta valresultat någonsin för att de har hamnat för mycket i mitten i politiken. Det menar Kjell Östberg, som forskar om socialdemokratin. – Det fungerar inte, säger Östberg i P1 Morgon. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Socialdemokraterna och Magdalena Andersson fick 28,02 procent av rösterna. 2,31 procentenheter sämre än förra valet – och det sämsta resultatet någonsin. En av förklaringarna tror Kjell Östberg, forskare i socialdemokrati vid Södertörns Högskola och medlem i Vänsterpartiet, handlar om att S har hamnat för mycket i mitten av politiken. – Socialdemokraterna har blivit ett ”catch all-parti”. Man vill lägga sig så nära de mittenpartierna som möjligt, men det fungerar inte, säger Östberg i P1 Morgon. Han menar att Socialdemokraterna har gått från att vara ett klassiskt arbetarklassparti med fokus på karensavdrag, arbetarpension och bankskatt till att snarare fokusera kring kriminalpolitik, migration och nationalism. Han lyfter motsvarigheterna i Tyskland och Danmark som exempel där samma strategi om att lägga sig närmre mitten har applicerats – och inneburit rekorddåliga resultat. – Skalet är kvar, men innehållet är i stora delar tömt. Med den politik man för nu, eller avsaknaden av den politik man för nu, så kommer de bli som alla andra partier av lite större styrka, säger Östberg. Stig-Björn Ljunggren, socialdemokratisk debattör, ledarskribent och statsvetare ser det däremot inte som ett lika stort problem. Han säger att borgerligheten har delats upp i två block – ett högerblock och ett ”allmänborgerligt” block. – Och det är där man ska ligga om man vill ha framgång. Satsar man enbart på arbetarklassen hamnar man ungefär där Vänsterpartiet har hamnat, säger han i P1.

articles.summary: Liam Nebel, som misstänks för attacken mot Brinellskolan, begärdes under måndagen häktad för fler brott, rapporterar Fagersta-Posten.
articles.body_text: Liam Nebel, som misstänks för attacken mot Brinellskolan, häktas misstänkt för fler brott, rapporterar Fagersta-Posten. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Det har gått en månad sedan attacken på Brinellskolan i Fagersta, där en flicka dödades och tre pojkar skadades. Den misstänkte, 18-årige Liam Nebel , sitter sedan dess frihetsberövad. På måndagen begärs han återigen häktad, misstänkt för fler brott än tidigare. Det har tidigare handlat om ett fall av mord och ett fall av mordförsök. Nu rör det sig om ytterligare två fall av mordförsök, rapporterar Fagersta-Posten. Rätten beslutade att han ska häktas för de nya brotten, skriver tidningen. Åklagaren har även begärt och fått godkännande av åtalsförlängning. Sammanlagt är 21 personer målsägande i fallet. Det är fler än vad det var för bara några dagar sedan. Då räknades tolv personer som förmodade brottsoffer, enligt VLT. En 16-årig pojke sitter också häktad misstänkt för medhjälp till mord. Nu häktas han för medhjälp till två fall av försök till mord, enligt Fagersta-Posten. Samma pojke misstänks även för förberedelse till mord, efter att ha planerat ett dåd mot sin egen skola, enligt uppgifter till flera medier. Båda två omhäktades för de första fallen av mord och mordförsök, samt medhjälp till mord och mordförsök, under måndagseftermiddagen. – Tingsrättens beslut idag gör att båda personerna nu är häktade misstänkta för brott kopplade till den avlidne målsäganden och de tre målsägandena som skadats i samband med händelsen på Brinellskolan i Fagersta den 21 augusti. Ett intensivt arbete pågår genom bland annat att förhör hålls, tekniska undersökningar genomförs och material analyseras, säger åklagare Ann-Sofie Trossing i ett pressmeddelande. articles.title: Ygeman: Försöka få ihop det här | Expressen
articles.summary: Den 13 september går Sverige till val. Följ Expressens direktrapport med senaste nytt inför valet.
articles.body_text: S-toppen Anders Ygeman befinner sig nu utanför Socialdemokraternas lokaler på Sveavägen 68. Han är fåordig med hur partiets arbete fortgår efter att Magdalena Andersson i fredags fick uppdrag att försöka bilda regering. – Nu får vi ta det lite lugnt, och försöka få ihop det här, säger han till Expressens reporter Nina Svanberg. Hur ska det gå då? – Det återstår att se. På frågan om vad man gör just nu, svarar han "ingen kommentar". Moderaterna kommer på nytt ha sina gruppmöten i den anrika förstakammarsalen i riksdagen. Där har SD suttit under förra mandatperioden. Den nya mandatfördelningen i riksdagen gör att några partier vuxit med andra krympt. SD tappade elva mandat i valet och landade på 62, medan Moderaterna ökade två mandat till 70 platser. Det gör att M tar tillbaka förstakammarsalen i riksdagens östra hus, uppger riksdagsdirektör Ingvar Mattson för TT. Där kommer partiet att ha sina gruppmöten. SD kommer att flytta in i ett annat mötesrum i Ledamotshuset, vilket SVT var först med att rapportera om. Civilminister Erik Slottner (KD) kommer inte få en plats i riksdagen, rapporterar Altinget. Han är därmed den tredje ministern i den nuvarande regeringen som inte väljs in. Sedan tidigare har det blivit känt att varken landsbygdsminister Peter Kullgren (KD) eller infrastruktur- och bostadsministern Andreas Carlson (KD) inte kommer in i riksdagen. Magdalena Andersson riktar i ett inlägg på Instagram kritik mot de senaste dagarnas diskussion om att många väljare i utanförskapsområden röstade rött. "Man har talat om 'röstboskap' och pekat ut enskilda grupper som ett demokratiskt problem." "Jag kommer alltid att stå upp för alla människors lika värde och för vår demokrati. För att hålla ihop vårt land. De senaste dagarna har politiska krafter till höger agerat på ett rent förkastligt sätt, genom att nära nog ifrågasätta vissa svenska medborgares röster", skriver s-ledaren. I förmiddags var rösterna färdigräknade. Nu har Valmyndigheten även kunnat fastställa det slutgiltiga valresultatet, skriver man i ett pressmeddelande.
